What the Bosnian Serbs wanted to do was have the territory that they had seized and were actually, while I was in Bosnia, still completing the ethnic cleansing; that is, ethnic cleansing in the area to the south-west of Banja Luka and ethnic cleansing of the enclaves in Srebrenica, Kamenica, Zepa, Gorazde. They, the Bosnian Serbs, were trying to secure what they had seized through force of arms. They therefore wanted a global cease-fire through all of Bosnia in order to consolidate what they had seized. The Muslims had lost that territory and did not want that situation to be recognised and to become a solid reality so therefore did not want a global cease-fire. In reality, though, they, for political reasons, would say that they did want a global cease-fire. They therefore would try to carry out local attacks, and then when they came under pressure, then they wanted a local cease-fire. Though they said they wanted global cease-fires, it is my belief - and it is General Morillon's understanding - that in practice they wanted to continue the fighting. That is the broad context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you believe that you were informed about the war objectives of both sides, and if that is so, what according to you was the war objective of the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER
utterances.text: My understanding of the war objective of the Muslim side was to re-establish the multi-ethnic country of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which had been given international recognition in -- early in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And whose territories did the Serbs capture during the war? From whom did they take these territories that they captured during the war?

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER
utterances.text: The Serbs -- the Bosnian Serbs seized territory which they claimed they were justified in seizing, and there was a meeting in Pale in November 1992 when General Morillon, myself, and Dr. Karadzic, General Mladic, and Professor Koljevic were all present. And at that meeting Dr. Karadzic got out a map which showed the ethnic distribution in all the parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and he stated that the Bosnian Serbs had only seized those territories to which they had a right, which was territories where the population was more than 50 per cent Bosnian Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can it be said then that the Serbs took territory from themselves in which we -- they were the majority population and in which, according to the elections, they held majority rule?

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of what the result of any elections were, so I cannot comment on the majority rule. What I can state is that the territory that the Serbs took, that they attacked and expelled non-Bosnian Serb citizens from those areas in what has come to be known as the practice of ethnic cleansing and that the removal of non-Bosnian Serb people from areas that the Serbs claimed for themselves was conducted in a brutal -- and in many times resulted in the deaths and extreme discomforts of many innocent civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this something that you saw for yourself or you believe the passage from the indictment that asserts that same thing? Do you have the results of the inquiry which established what you have just said?

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER
utterances.text: I have seen for myself the results of the ethnic cleansing in the area to the south-west of Banja Luka, and I saw for myself the ethnic cleansing that took place in the Srebrenica enclave in March, which is described in my statements, and I, in my position as military assistant to General Morillon, was in receipt of all the reports prepared through the military chain of command of UNPROFOR in Bosnia and thus received reports of all occasions when UNPROFOR forces, soldiers, saw ethnic cleansing taking place or saw the results where ethnic cleansing had taken place. The last source of information was from UNHCR when UNHCR personnel had seen or witnessed ethnic cleansing taking place or the results of ethnic cleansing that had previously taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will come to that. We will deal with this tomorrow. Let me ask you this: Do you know what a constituent peoples, what that term means in our context? There were three such peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina, to help you. Let me ask you this: Do you know that no decision can be made in constitutional issues without the agreement of all of the three constituent peoples who were part of the constituent state? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER
utterances.text: I am a military officer who was serving with the United Nations, and what you are describing is not something that came into my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, but were you familiar with the political life and the circumstances before the war and that we could have stopped the secession of Bosnia-Herzegovina by refusing to agree to it and that we did agree to it with one condition? Did you know that? Did you know that there was a peace conference that was held before the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER
utterances.text: I'm aware of all the reports which were carried in the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the European Community at the time, the European Community, offered a solution with which we would accept the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which implied the transformation of Bosnia and Herzegovina into three constituent states and that we accepted independence only with that condition?

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER
utterances.text: This lies outside my area of competence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But with all due respect, Mr. Tucker, you are saying some other things that are outside of your area of competence which do have political implications, and this is why I'm asking you if you had heard that on the 18th of March all three sides in Bosnia-Herzegovina accepted the Lisbon agreement under which Bosnia-Herzegovina would be independent but would have three constituent units, three administrations at the lower level and a common administration? Did you know this?

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Dr. Karadzic, but I am here to provide evidence about the time that I was in Bosnia. Events before my time in Bosnia or after my time in Bosnia are issues you must take up with people who are involved with those events.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, and excuse me, Dr. Karadzic. Before we recess, I just wanted to clarify our schedule for tomorrow because the witness had indicated when we had a meeting yesterday that he was not available for part of the day tomorrow and it might be worthwhile to deal with that before he leaves today, so if we can all make our plans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, having heard Mr. Robinson's intervention, could you let us know your position in relation to your travel plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have a board meeting which I need to attend by conference call between 2.00 and 3.00 tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a conference call, so I can take it by telephone from anywhere in this building. I just need a room in order to be able to make the telephone call and join the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would the next witness be available for that -- at 2.00 tomorrow afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I don't know, but I can certainly find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In one way or another, we'll try our best to accommodate your situation, sir. Noting the time, it's time to adjourn for today. We will resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 18th day of January, 2012, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.00 p.m.,
